Related software

Source: vignettes/related-software.Rmd
related-software.Rmd

This page places the package beside the ones a reader is likely to have used, with the argument of each that sets the same quantity, and says what each fits that this one does not.

The same quantity in each package

Quantity thiessen AddiVortes BART dbarts stochtree
ensemble size term_params(tessellations = ) m ntree ntree num_trees
cell or leaf prior spread term_params(k = ) k k k k
noise prior degrees of freedom gaussian_outcome(nu = ) nu sigdf sigdf
noise prior quantile gaussian_outcome(q = ) q sigquant sigquant
burn-in sweeps general_params(burn_in = ) mcmcBurnIn nskip nskip num_burnin
kept draws general_params(draws = ) totalMCMCIter - mcmcBurnIn ndpost ndpost num_mcmc
thinning general_params(thinning = ) keepevery keepevery
chains thiessen(chains = ) mc.wbart(mc.cores = ) nchain num_chains
threads thiessen(threads = ), mc.cores mc.cores nthread num_threads
seed thiessen(seed = ) set.seed() seed seed random_seed

The three rows with no counterpart in the tree packages are the tessellation’s own: sigma_c, the centre-coordinate scale (sd in AddiVortes); omega, the prior mean number of active covariates (Omega); and lambda_c, the cell-count prior rate (LambdaRate). A tree has no centres, and its depth prior plays the part of the cell-count prior.

What each package fits

AddiVortes is the authors’ implementation of the method, in R and C++. It is the reference this package is checked against: the test suite compares posterior summaries and the comparators harness in the repository checks realised cell counts and held-out summaries at release. This package adds the formula interface, the multi-chain diagnostics, the posterior and rstantools generics, persistence of a fit, and the sampler API; the models are the same.

BART (Sparapani, Spanbauer and McCulloch 2021) fits BART for continuous, binary, multinomial, survival (abart, surv.bart), competing-risks and recurrent-events outcomes, with the DART sparsity prior. Of those, this package’s published surface has the continuous and probit models; the accelerated-failure-time, Student-t, Laplace and DART variants exist behind the experimental build until each is calibrated and derived.

dbarts (Dorie and others) fits continuous and binary BART with a sampler object the caller can drive and modify between sweeps, the pattern this package’s thiessen_sampler() follows.

stochtree (Herren and others) fits BART and Bayesian causal forests with a low-level interface for custom sampling loops and a multi-chain page with R-hat and effective sample sizes; its bart() also takes a variance_forest_params for a heteroscedastic model, as variance_params does here.

bartMachine (Kapelner and Bleich 2016) fits continuous and binary BART in Java, with variable-selection procedures this package does not have.

rbart (Pratola and others) is HBART, the heteroscedastic tree model that H-AddiVortes follows; rbart::rbart(ntreeh = ) is variance_params here.

The Python package

The same core is wrapped for Python, with the same configuration names, a scikit-learn estimator pair and an arviz conversion; a fit saved by one binding is read by the other, and an integer seed gives the same draws in both. Its documentation is under python/ in the repository.

References

Chipman, H. A., George, E. I. and McCulloch, R. E. (2010). BART: Bayesian additive regression trees. The Annals of Applied Statistics 4(1), 266-298. doi:10.1214/09-AOAS285

Kapelner, A. and Bleich, J. (2016). bartMachine: machine learning with Bayesian additive regression trees. Journal of Statistical Software 70(4), 1-40. doi:10.18637/jss.v070.i04

Pratola, M. T., Chipman, H. A., George, E. I. and McCulloch, R. E. (2020). Heteroscedastic BART via multiplicative regression trees. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 29(2), 405-417. doi:10.1080/10618600.2019.1677243

Sparapani, R., Spanbauer, C. and McCulloch, R. (2021). Nonparametric machine learning and efficient computation with Bayesian additive regression trees: the BART R package. Journal of Statistical Software 97(1), 1-66. doi:10.18637/jss.v097.i01

Stone, A. and Gosling, J. P. (2025). AddiVortes: (Bayesian) additive Voronoi tessellations. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 34(3), 859-871. doi:10.1080/10618600.2024.2414104
